idiom_name: versioned TLV payload bound as a BLOB (sqlite3_bind_blob / sqlite3_column_blob)
implementation_notes: C has no reflection and no serializer in the standard library, so the pattern degenerates into a hand-written byte format: a format-version byte, then length-prefixed fields, bound as a BLOB with sqlite3_bind_blob (pass SQLITE_TRANSIENT so SQLite copies the buffer before it goes out of scope) and read back with sqlite3_column_blob plus sqlite3_column_bytes. Prefer explicit little-endian helpers over memcpy of the struct: padding, alignment and host byte order make raw struct dumps non-portable, and embedded pointers have to be replaced by copied data. The hand-written form stays justified for small private formats; once the entity evolves or interoperates, a schema-driven codec (protobuf-c, FlatBuffers, CBOR) is the honest replacement.
pitfalls: Never memcpy a struct into the column: padding and alignment bytes and host endianness differ between builds, so stored rows become unreadable elsewhere.
Pointers inside the struct are not part of the payload; deep-copy strings into the buffer on save and allocate owned copies on load, or you persist addresses.
Every decode parses stored bytes as untrusted input: validate lengths before advancing the cursor so a corrupted payload cannot overrun the buffer.
sqlite3_bind_blob's destructor argument controls buffer lifetime - SQLITE_STATIC keeps a reference to your memory until step or reset, which breaks if the buffer is freed early.
